newsitem.title: UK: Wellington agrees bid for Premium.
newsitem.headline: Wellington agrees bid for Premium.

text.p: Wellington Underwriting Plc said on Monday it had made a recommended offer for Premium Underwriting Plc, valuing the company at 34.9 million stg.

Wellington said in a statement that it is offering 125 new Wellington shares and 25.20 stg for every 100 ordinary Premium shares. This represents a premium of 37.2 percent over Premium's closing price on January 15, the day before the announcement by Premium that it was in talks which might lead to an offer.

The company said the enlarged group will be one of the major specialist Lloyd's insurance groups managing over 600 million stg capacity and owning 142 million of allocated capacity of which some 54 percent is allocated to the Wellington Syndicates.
Wellington has received an an irrevocable undertaking to accept the convertible offer from a shareholder owning around 94 percent of Premium convertible shares.
It expects the acquisition to be broadly earnings neutral in 1997 but predicts it will enhance earnings in 1998.
"This transaction allows Wellington to increase earnings and assets per share while more than doubling our underwriting capacity," said Antony Haynes, chairman of Wellington.
